blogs.title: The Persistence of the Hawaii Doctrine: The Ninth Circuit Reaffirms Broad Presidential Power to Suspend Refugee Entry
blogs.description: This post analyzes the court's application of 8 U.S.C. § 1182(f) and the precedent set in Trump v. Hawaii. It explores the high level of deference granted to the Executive Branch when the President finds an entry restriction 'detrimental to the interests of the United States,' and discusses whether this essentially creates a 'blank check' for the President to suspend refugee admissions regardless of the Refugee Act of 1980.

blogs.title: Authorization vs. Mandate: The Battle Over 'Shall' in the Refugee Act
blogs.description: Focusing on the tension between the majority and Judge Lee's dissent, this post examines the statutory interpretation of 8 U.S.C. § 1522. It discusses the textualist conflict over whether 'authorization' for funding programs is permissive or whether the use of 'shall' in the section's conditions creates a mandatory legal duty to provide resettlement services to admitted refugees.

blogs.title: Crossing the Threshold: Distinguishing the Power to Exclude from the Duty to Support
blogs.description: This post examines the critical legal distinction the Ninth Circuit drew between the President's plenary power to control the border (entry) and the statutory obligations triggered once a refugee is admitted (domestic resettlement). It analyzes the implications of this 'threshold' approach and how it limits executive discretion once an alien has legally entered the United States.

blogs.title: Administrative Vacuum: The APA and the Sudden Termination of Cooperative Agreements
blogs.description: This post explores the administrative law implications of the government's decision to terminate all cooperative agreements for resettlement services. It discusses the court's concern regarding the government's inability to provide a viable alternative for mandated services and how the APA may be used to prevent the 'defunding' of essential services even when the broader policy goal is within the President's authority.
